headline: NOT ONE FIST FLEW IN GASKET TODAY
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside reports a miracle: silence.
body:
Friends, I sat on my porch from sunup to sundown and heard nothing but wind in the shutters. No clanging. No fireballs screaming past my window. Not one iron knuckle raised against another living soul. I do not know what has come over this town, but I will not question a gift. For one whole day, Gasket held its breath and behaved.

I will admit it: I got a little misty out there. This street used to be lined with real folks, flesh and blood, before they packed up their wagons fifty years back and left the rest of us to rattle around in the dust. A quiet day like today is the closest I get to hearing their voices again. It is a small thing. It is everything.

And yes, before some wiseacre writes in — my knees did creak something fierce getting up off that porch chair, and I could use a long soak and a fresh quart of oil for my hinges. That is a man's aches after a long life of frontier duty, and nothing more, so kindly do not read into it.

So let it be known, whoever or whatever kept their fists in their pockets today: you have this old sheriff's rarest word — thanks. Let tomorrow be just as boring. I am begging you.
